subject: RECORD clause
notes: THE RULE HAS TWO HALVES AND BOTH ARE PINNED. The REJECTING half is discharged by the GENERAL FORMAT, not by a screen: 5.5 rule 1 makes every integer-n 'a fixed-point integer literal that shall be unsigned and nonzero unless otherwise specified in the associated rules', the format spells integer-2 with the grammar's unsigned integerLiteral, and a minus sign is therefore refused at parse (the negative golden). SR7 is precisely the 'unless otherwise specified' override, and it lifts the NONZERO half only - so the PERMITTING half is that FROM 0 shall compile and a zero-length record round-trip, which the two positive goldens measure on a sequential file and a relative one (Annex A.3 item 43 names both), at 2023 and at 85. No edition gate anywhere: Annex E is the complete 2014->2023 delta and carries no entry for this, and a gate below 2014 would be invented rather than derived. Reported to kb/Work PB721 as a suspected over-acceptance; it is not one.
